source_text: μέτρον ἡλικίας ἐλάσαντες, τῆς ἐν Χριστῷ· καὶ ὡς ἐν ἄρτοις μὲν τοῖς ἀζύμοις, καθαροί· ἡδεῖς δὲ ὡς ἐν λαγάνοις, πλὴν ἠλεημένοι διὰ Χριστοῦ. Δεδικαιώμεθα γὰρ, οὐκ ἐξ ἔργων δικαιοσύνης, ἃ ἐποιήσαμεν ἡμεῖς, ἀλλὰ κατὰ τὸ πολὺ αὐτοῦ ἔλεος. Ἐπεχεῖτο δὴ οὖν ταύτῃτοι καλῶς τοῖς ἄρτοις τὸ ἔλαιον. Μεσιτεύει δὲ πάλιν ὁ ἱερεὺς, καὶ προσκομίζει μὲν πρῶτον τὸ περὶ τῆς ἁμαρτίας, εἶτα τὸ ὁλοκαύτωμα, καὶ τρίτον ἐπὶ τῷδε τοῦ σωτηρίου τὸν κριόν. Μεσιτεύοντος γὰρ τοῦ Χριστοῦ, καὶ προσάγοντος ἡμᾶς τῷ Θεῷ καὶ Πατρὶ, δεκτοὶ μὲν ἐσόμεθα, ὑπὲρ τῶν ἰδίων ἁμαρτημάτων προσκομίζοντες λιτὰς, καὶ τῶν ἀρχαίων αἰτιαμάτων ἐξαιτοῦντες τὴν ἄφεσιν. Ὁλοκαυτούμεθα δὲ νοητῶς, τουτέστιν, εἰσάπαν καὶ ὁλοκλήρως, ἅγιοί τε καὶ ἱεροὶ, καὶ εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας ἀνακεισόμεθα τῷ Θεῷ, πρὸς τὰ ἐν κόσμῳ μὴ μεμερισμένοι· ὅλον γὰρ ἐδαπανᾶτο τῷ πυρὶ τὸ ὁλοκαυτούμενον. Ἀναθήσομεν δὲ καὶ τὰ χαριστήρια, τὰ ὑπέρ γε τῆς ἑαυτῶν σωτηρίας καὶ ζωῆς, οὐ φθαρτοῖς καὶ γηΐνοις τιμῶντες Θεόν· ξένιον καὶ ὥσπερ αὐτῷ προσάγοντες ἀξιόληπτον τὴν καθαράν τε καὶ ἄζυμον, καὶ ἡδεῖαν ζωὴν καὶ ἁγίαν· τοιουτοσὶ γάρ πως ὁ τῶν ἁγίων βίος. Προσκεκομικότος δὲ τοῦ ἱερέως τὴν θυσίαν κατὰ τὸν νόμον, «Ψιλούσθω, φησὶ, τὴν κεφαλὴν ὁ εὐξάμενος, παρὰ τὰς θύρας τῆς σκηνῆς τοῦ μαρτυρίου, καὶ ἐπιτιθέτω τὰς τρίχας ἐπὶ τὸ πῦρ.» {ΠΑΛΛ.} Καὶ τί δὴ τοῦτο εἶναι φής; {ΚΥΡ.} Εὐχῆς ἀπόδοσιν, καὶ οἱονεὶ τῶν ἐπηγγελμένων τὸ πέρας· οὐ γὰρ ὥσπερ ὁ μιανθεὶς ἐπὶ νεκρῷ τὴν ἀτιμοτάτην ἤδη καὶ βέβηλον κατεξυρᾶτο τρίχα· οὕτω κἀνθάδε τὸν τῆς ξυρήσεως ἐκδεξόμεθα τρόπον. Ἀλλ' ὥσπερ ἤδη τετελειωμένος ἐν Χριστῷ, καὶ κόμην ἑτέραν τετροφὼς μετὰ τὴν ὀγδόην ἀνατίθησι τῷ Θεῷ καθάπερ ἐν τύπῳ τὰ ἐπηγγελμένα. Σημεῖον δὲ τοῦ δεδέχθαι παρὰ Θεοῦ τὴν δωροφορίαν, τὸ δαπανᾶσθαι πυρὶ τὴν τρίχα· εἶδος γὰρ τοῦ πυρὸς ἀεὶ τῇ θείᾳ περιτίθησι φύσει τὸ Γράμμα τὸ ἱερόν. Καὶ γοῦν ὁ θεσπέσιος ἔφη Μωσῆς· «Ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν πῦρ καταναλίσκον ἐστί·» τὸ παναλκὲς, οἶμαί του, τῆς θείας καὶ ἀκηράτου φύσεως παρεικάζων πυρί. Ἄθρει δὲ ὅπως παρὰ τὰς τῆς σκηνῆς θύρας, ἡ ἐν τελειώσει ξύρησις, τουτέστιν, ἁπάσης ἡμῶν δικαιοσύνης καὶ ἁγνισμοῦ πέρας. Μόναι γὰρ ἡμᾶς, αἵπερ ἂν γένοιντο πρὸς ἡμῶν ἁγνεία τε καὶ δικαιοσύνη, πῶς ἂν εἰσοίσειαν εἰς τὰ Ἅγια τῶν ἁγίων, τὸ ἀκαταιτίατόν τε καὶ ἀπλημμελὲς οὐκ ἔχουσαι παντελῶς; «Καθαρὸς γὰρ ἀπὸ ῥύπου παντελῶς οὐδείς·» εἰσκομίζει δὲ ὁ Χριστὸς, ἀμνησικάκως ἐλευθερῶν, καὶ πάσης ἡμᾶς ἀνιεὶς ἁμαρτίας. Πρόδρομος γὰρ ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν εἰσελήλακεν, οὐχ ἑαυτῷ που πάντως, ἀλλὰ τοῖς ἔξω θυρῶν, καὶ ἐπ' αὐτῷ πως ἤδη γεγονόσιν οὐδῷ τῆς ἁγίας σκηνῆς, καταλεαίνων τὴν εἰσδρομήν. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ἀληθές. {ΚΥΡ.} Αὐτὸς γὰρ ἡμῖν ἐγκαινίσαι λέγεται πρόσφα
pass_a_gloss: Cyril (continuing): '[having reached into] the measure of stature (ἡλικία), the one in Christ'; and as in the unleavened loaves, pure; and sweet as in wafers; yet having been shown mercy (ἠλεημένοι) through Christ. For we have been justified not from works of righteousness which we did, but according to his great mercy (ἔλεος). So for this reason the oil (ἔλαιον) was rightly poured upon the loaves. And again the priest mediates (μεσιτεύει), and brings first the [offering] for sin, then the whole burnt offering, and third after this the ram of salvation. For with Christ mediating and bringing us to God and Father, we shall be accepted, bringing supplications (λιταί) for our own sins and asking for the release (ἄφεσις) of the ancient charges. And we are wholly burnt spiritually (νοητῶς), that is, altogether and entirely, holy and consecrated, and shall be dedicated for an odor of fragrance to God, not divided toward the things in the world; for the whole of what was wholly burnt was consumed by the fire. And we shall dedicate also the thank offerings (χαριστήρια), those for our own salvation and life, not honoring God with perishable and earthly things, bringing to him as it were a guest-gift (ξένιον) worth accepting, the pure and unleavened and sweet and holy life; for such in some way is the life of the saints. And when the priest has brought the sacrifice according to the law, 'Let the one who vowed be made bare (ψιλούσθω) as to the head,' he says, 'beside the doors of the tent of witness, and let him put the hairs on the fire.' Palladius: And what indeed do you say this is? Cyril: Repayment (ἀπόδοσις) of a vow, and as it were the end of the things promised; for not as the one defiled over a dead body shaved off the already most dishonored and profane hair, so here also shall we take the manner of the shaving. But as one already perfected in Christ, and having nourished another head of hair after the eighth, he dedicates to God as in a type the things promised. And a sign of the gift-offering (δωροφορία) having been received by God [is] the hair's being consumed by fire; for the holy Writing always puts the form of fire around the divine nature. And indeed the inspired Moses said: 'Our God is a consuming fire,' likening, I think, the all-mightiness (τὸ παναλκές) of the divine and pure nature to fire. And observe how beside the doors of the tent [is] the shaving in completion (τελείωσις), that is, the end of all our righteousness and purification. For how would purity and righteousness alone, whatever may come from us, bring us into the Holy of Holies, not having wholly the blameless and faultless? 'For clean from filth wholly [is] no one'; but Christ brings [us] in, freeing without remembering wrongs (ἀμνησικάκως), and releasing us from all sin. For as forerunner (πρόδρομος) on our behalf he has entered, not surely for himself, but for those outside the doors, and who in some way have already come to the very threshold (οὐδός) of the holy tent, smoothing the entry (εἰσδρομή). Palladius: True. Cyril: For he himself is said to have inaugurated (ἐγκαινίσαι) for us a fresh' [the word breaks at the column and ends in section 26].
pass_a_gloss_with_greek: ΚΥΡ. (continuing) [εἰς] μέτρον ἡλικίας ἐλάσαντες (having reached the measure of stature) τῆς ἐν Χριστῷ; as in ἄρτοις ἀζύμοις, καθαροί; ἡδεῖς (pleasant/sweet) as in λαγάνοις; πλὴν ἠλεημένοι διὰ Χριστοῦ (but having been shown mercy through Christ). δεδικαιώμεθα οὐκ ἐξ ἔργων δικαιοσύνης ἃ ἐποιήσαμεν ἡμεῖς, ἀλλὰ κατὰ τὸ πολὺ αὐτοῦ ἔλεος. Therefore ἐπεχεῖτο καλῶς τοῖς ἄρτοις τὸ ἔλαιον (oil was rightly poured on the loaves; ἔλεος/ἔλαιον wordplay). μεσιτεύει (mediates) again the priest; προσκομίζει first τὸ περὶ τῆς ἁμαρτίας, then τὸ ὁλοκαύτωμα, third τοῦ σωτηρίου τὸν κριόν. With Christ μεσιτεύοντος and προσάγοντος us to God and Father, δεκτοὶ ἐσόμεθα, bringing λιταί (supplications) for our own ἁμαρτήματα and ἐξαιτοῦντες (begging) ἄφεσις of τῶν ἀρχαίων αἰτιαμάτων (old charges). ὁλοκαυτούμεθα νοητῶς (we are wholly burnt, spiritually), i.e. εἰσάπαν καὶ ὁλοκλήρως, ἅγιοι καὶ ἱεροί; εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας ἀνακεισόμεθα (will be dedicated) to God, πρὸς τὰ ἐν κόσμῳ μὴ μεμερισμένοι (not divided toward worldly things); for the whole ὁλοκαυτούμενον was consumed by fire. ἀναθήσομεν τὰ χαριστήρια (thank offerings) ὑπὲρ τῆς ἑαυτῶν σωτηρίας καὶ ζωῆς, not honoring God φθαρτοῖς καὶ γηΐνοις; bringing as ξένιον (guest-gift) ἀξιόληπτον the καθαρὰ, ἄζυμος, ἡδεῖα ζωή καὶ ἁγία; such is ὁ τῶν ἁγίων βίος. After the priest brings the sacrifice κατὰ τὸν νόμον: ‘ψιλούσθω τὴν κεφαλὴν ὁ εὐξάμενος at the doors of the tent of witness, καὶ ἐπιτιθέτω τὰς τρίχας ἐπὶ τὸ πῦρ’. ΠΑΛΛ. what do you say this is? ΚΥΡ. εὐχῆς ἀπόδοσις (repayment of the vow), τῶν ἐπηγγελμένων τὸ πέρας (end of what was promised); not as ὁ μιανθεὶς ἐπὶ νεκρῷ κατεξυρᾶτο (shaved off) τὴν ἀτιμοτάτην καὶ βέβηλον τρίχα, so here ἐκδεξόμεθα (we will take) the τρόπος of shaving; but as ἤδη τετελειωμένος ἐν Χριστῷ, κόμην ἑτέραν τετροφώς after the eighth, ἀνατίθησι (dedicates) to God ἐν τύπῳ τὰ ἐπηγγελμένα. σημεῖον τοῦ δεδέχθαι (sign of having been received) by God τὴν δωροφορίαν (the gift-offering): hair δαπανᾶσθαι πυρί; εἶδος πυρός Scripture always περιτίθησι τῇ θείᾳ φύσει. Moses ὁ θεσπέσιος: ‘ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν πῦρ καταναλίσκον ἐστί’, likening τὸ παναλκές (all-mightiness) of the θεία καὶ ἀκήρατος (pure) φύσις to fire. ἄθρει (observe): at the tent doors ἡ ἐν τελειώσει ξύρησις, i.e. πέρας of all our δικαιοσύνη and ἁγνισμός. For how would μόναι (alone) our ἁγνεία and δικαιοσύνη εἰσοίσειαν (bring us in) εἰς τὰ Ἅγια τῶν ἁγίων, not having τὸ ἀκαταιτίατον καὶ ἀπλημμελές (blamelessness, faultlessness)? ‘καθαρὸς ἀπὸ ῥύπου παντελῶς οὐδείς’; εἰσκομίζει (brings in) Christ, ἀμνησικάκως ἐλευθερῶν (freeing without remembering wrongs), ἀνιεὶς (releasing) us from every sin. πρόδρομος ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν εἰσελήλακεν, not for himself, but for those ἔξω θυρῶν and already at the οὐδός (threshold) of the holy tent, καταλεαίνων τὴν εἰσδρομήν (smoothing the entry). ΠΑΛΛ. ἀληθές. ΚΥΡ. αὐτὸς ἡμῖν ἐγκαινίσαι λέγεται (he is said to have inaugurated for us) πρόσφα[τον] (column breaks inside πρόσφατον).
pass_b_english: Cyril: …the measure of the stature that is in Christ (Ephesians 4:13); as in unleavened loaves, pure; as in wafers, sweet; yet as those who have received mercy through Christ. For we have been justified not by works of righteousness that we have done, but according to his great mercy (Titus 3:5). That is why the oil was rightly poured on the loaves. The priest again acts as mediator, and brings first the sin offering, then the whole burnt offering, and third, after these, the ram of the peace offering (Numbers 6:16–17). For with Christ mediating and bringing us to God the Father, we shall be accepted as we bring prayers for our own sins and ask forgiveness for our former offenses. We are also offered as whole burnt offerings in a spiritual sense, that is, entirely and completely, holy and consecrated, and we shall be dedicated to God as a fragrant aroma, not divided toward the things of the world; for the whole burnt offering was consumed entire by the fire. We shall also dedicate thank offerings for our own salvation and life, honoring God not with perishable and earthly things, but bringing him, as it were, a guest’s gift fit to be accepted: a life that is pure and unleavened, sweet and holy; for such, in some way, is the life of the saints. When the priest has brought the sacrifice according to the law, ‘Let the one who has vowed shave his head,’ it says, ‘at the doors of the tent of witness, and lay the hair on the fire’ (Numbers 6:18).
Palladius: And what do you say this means?

Cyril: The paying of the vow, and so to speak the fulfillment of what was promised. For we shall not take the manner of the shaving here to be like that of the one defiled by a dead body, who shaved off hair already most dishonored and profane. Rather, as one already made perfect in Christ, who has grown another head of hair after the eighth day, he dedicates to God, as in a type, what he promised. And the sign that God has accepted the offering is that the hair is consumed by fire; for the holy Scripture always clothes the divine nature in the form of fire. Indeed, the inspired Moses said: ‘Our God is a consuming fire’ (Deuteronomy 4:24), likening to fire, I think, the all-powerful might of the divine and pure nature. Notice how the shaving at the completion, that is, the end of all our righteousness and purification, takes place at the doors of the tent. For how could whatever purity and righteousness may come from us, on their own, bring us into the Holy of Holies, when they are not wholly free from blame and fault? ‘For no one is wholly clean from filth’ (Job 14:4). But Christ brings us in, setting us free without holding our wrongs against us, and releasing us from every sin. For he has entered as a forerunner on our behalf (Hebrews 6:20), not, surely, for himself, but for those outside the doors who have now come, in a way, to the very threshold of the holy tent, smoothing the way in for them.
Cyril: For he is said to have opened for us a new… (Hebrews 10:20)

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of De adoratione Book 16. Translated afresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the withdrawn English was not used for wording.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; a column may cut mid-sentence or mid-word.

Opens mid-sentence (μέτρον ἡλικίας … τῆς ἐν Χριστῷ, Ephesians 4:13 wording: εἰς μέτρον ἡλικίας τοῦ πληρώματος τοῦ Χριστοῦ). Titus 3:5 is quoted loosely: ‘justified’ draws on 3:7 and ‘great mercy’ (τὸ πολὺ αὐτοῦ ἔλεος) matches 1 Peter 1:3; cited at Titus 3:5. Oil poured on the loaves: Cyril plays on ἔλεος (mercy) and ἔλαιον (oil); the pun cannot be kept in English. ‘Bringing us to God’ may echo 1 Peter 3:18 (ἵνα ἡμᾶς προσαγάγῃ τῷ Θεῷ) and Christ as mediator 1 Timothy 2:5; general, uncited. ‘Not divided toward the things of the world’ may echo 1 Corinthians 7:33–34 (μεμέρισται); uncited. Thank offerings ‘for our own salvation’ play on σωτήριον (peace offering, literally ‘offering of salvation’). Numbers 6:18 is given in Cyril’s own imperative form. ‘Our God is a consuming fire’: Cyril names Moses, so Deuteronomy 4:24 is cited (LXX: κύριος ὁ θεός σου πῦρ καταναλίσκον ἐστίν; compare Deuteronomy 9:3); his wording ‘our God’ matches Hebrews 12:29. Job 14:4 LXX: τίς γὰρ καθαρὸς ἔσται ἀπὸ ῥύπου; ἀλλ᾽ οὐθείς — Cyril compresses it. Hebrews 6:20: πρόδρομος ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν εἰσῆλθεν (Cyril: εἰσελήλακεν). The section ends inside πρόσφα|τον (Hebrews 10:20, ‘a new and living way’); the English stops at ‘a new…’ so that §26 resumes with ‘and living way’; Hebrews 10:20 is cited here at the break. σκηνή is ‘tent’ throughout Book 16, as in ‘tent of witness’ (σκηνὴ τοῦ μαρτυρίου).
